title: “Leadership Is What Matters Most in a School” https://www.educationnext.org/leadership-is-what-matters-most-in-a-school-interview-greg-richmond/
author: Greg Richmond
summary: In an Education Next interview, Greg Richmond reflects on leading in three sectors: district schools in Chicago, charter authorizing nationally, and five years as superintendent of the Archdiocese of Chicago's Catholic schools. His main claim is that the school, not the classroom or system, is the unit of change, and that leadership is what matters most in a school. Governance, autonomy, regulation, and choice are tailwinds or headwinds, but they cannot substitute for a strong leader. He explains how administrative and compliance demands reduce a principal's time as an instructional leader, giving an example of removing a burdensome video requirement. He compares sectors on money, politics, parent engagement, mission clarity, and service to students with special needs. He also stresses belonging and school culture as drivers of achievement and says choice alone cannot deliver good instruction.
points: Richmond argues that the school is the unit of change because an individual excellent teacher in a weak culture will remain an outlier.
Leadership is the decisive factor, and external structures such as choice or autonomy only make success easier or harder.
Heavy compliance demands pull principals away from instructional leadership, and teachers then retreat behind closed doors, eroding alignment and rigor.
His cross-sector comparison finds Catholic schools strong on parent engagement and cost-consciousness, charters on clear mission, and districts on serving students with the greatest needs.
He treats belonging as a cultural outcome that adults create deliberately or by neglect, and says choice is a tailwind rather than a guarantee of quality.
quotes: I have long believed that the school—more than the classroom or system—is the unit of change in reform and that school culture is a critical driver of improvement.
As with any organization, I believe leadership is what matters most in a school.
Tailwinds alone cannot produce an excellent school in the absence of a strong leader.
The more such demands you place on a principal, the less time she has to be an instructional leader.
One principal said to me, “I guarantee you that no child has ever found Jesus because of those videos.
every school has a culture and norms about how people treat each other. The adults in the school create that culture, either positively and on purpose, or negatively through lack of attention.
It is a good tailwind that enables high-quality instruction, but choice itself does not deliver high-quality instruction. It is the adults in the school who do that.
